key_insight: SoftServe is a scalable quasi-Newton family that keeps curvature estimates positive definite by construction, making second-order-style optimization practical for deep learning.
engineering_relevance: It targets large, ill-conditioned neural training problems by avoiding line searches and matrix decompositions, using GPU-friendly coupled Newton-Schulz iterations instead.
method: Derives positive-definite curvature from a variational objective, even when true curvature is negative.
Provides diagonal and Kronecker-factored variants for large-scale neural networks.
Uses stable coupled Newton-Schulz iterations for matrix operations instead of expensive decompositions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong results on ill-conditioned benchmarks, including recurrent networks, deep autoencoders, physics-informed neural networks, and a 136M-parameter physics-informed diffusion model, often outperforming Adam, Muon, and SOAP.
watch_item: As with many quasi-Newton methods, practical performance may depend on numerical stability and the cost/quality tradeoff of curvature approximations at very large scale.
paper_title: SoftServe: A Scalable Quasi-Newton Method for Deep Learning
